Ps. See the below from a friend. 
Yesterday I did a fireside chat at a conference. And while I'm sitting here on my flight home, thought I 
would share some of the content and how it relates to a couple of thoughts about the consumer 
technology world, and hope one of your lovely minds can help me refine them. Long flight, long post. 
What I shared was the emergence of a new operating system for mankind that could be characterized as 
Collaborative Non-Conformity, a global affinity and dependence on diversity, and see it as the simple 
confluence of increasing worldwide connectivity through technology and growing individual 
accountability across our communities. In other words, public and referenceable identities and 
experiences, and access to more tools than ever that allow us to communicate, trade, self-publish and 
provide feedback on those identities and experiences. 
I see this as an opportunity to witness a practical participatory economy take shape, with a generation of 
empowered individuals operating outside the shadows creating a new framework for humanity to 
amplify and celebrate our differences on this beautiful playground of spaceship Earth, and perhaps 
beyond. To be respectful of nature as they lay the Fabric of Wisdom on the Information Age. But, it 
could also go the other way (I will mention without caution on that below). 
//What is happening?// 
While our generation and the ones before us began our lives building friendships and finding our tribes 
in physical space, our children, or Generation (N)ow as I call them, are starting their lives and finding 
their tribes in digital space. They find like-mindedness earlier, and find them from a larger pool. As a 
generation, this empowers them to embrace their uniqueness more than ever before possible, at a 
EFTA01050453
--- PAGE 2 ---
younger age than ever before. 
Gen N are also entering this world with a keener awareness of being part of a connected species. Up 
until now, we have each come into this world concerned primarily with our navigable physical space. As 
we have become more connected, our voices travel further and our information comes from across the 
world, through channels we have curated for ourselves (the age of mass media is increasingly behind us). 
Generation Z is the last transition generation. After them, a majority of souls coming into physicality will 
grow up primarily communicating, exchanging ideas, and forging relationships with others beyond 
geographical or nationalistic boundaries. 
While we have lived and built mostly physical lives and sought to bring expressions of them online, Gen 
N are beginning their time on Earth with digital identities, with corporations and governments charting 
their growth and experiences without their conscious choice to have it be so. Their new battle is not 
primarily for money but instead more social relevance and credibility in the form of an audience and 
owned digital content. Oh the stress! 
As this digital shift brings our identities online, Gen N are developing a global accountability of their 
actions, as everything is increasingly digitized and stored (Internet of Things, ubiquitous sensors, etc). 
They are also starting to have access to a global hive mind to look to for solutions, as we each become 
publishers, and crowdsourced data feeds into the variety of machine learning algorithms and A.I. 
projects that seek to answer our health, economic and scientific questions. 
//V/here must we invest? - Building trust in an untrustworthy world// 
Is our obligation and burden to build and leave tools and structures that we think support Generation 
ability to thrive in this seemingly complex world they are coming into? No! That's obnoxious to think we 
know what's best for them. Our obligation is to watch them, and learn from them. Allow them space to 
build trust with one another. This is a generation that will lead us into a collective living environment 
that is conscious and tolerant as long as we don't hold them hostage to our old ways of thinking about 
our definitions of personal and collective success! 
What we should invest in and conserve are spaces for them to play within and between tribes, to explore 
the connectivity with each other and nature and the self-actualization they will inevitably confront. 
Because we are humans, and we are physical. Until we can mimic a completely realistic physical 
environment in virtual space (hrmm... but worth trying), they need real places to commune and celebrate 
their digital tribes. They are already asking for this. Look at the rise in meetup culture and festival 
culture and youth conferences all across the planet. They are already looking for their playgrounds to 
meet with their digital communities that share the same appreciation for music, art, science, nature and 
everything else (scarily even VidCon). I'm looking actively to support the creation and protection of 
these spaces and events. 
They will seek out places to live together. Aggregated not by our old world notions of what matters, tied 
often to productivity and economics (fuck co-working), but instead aggregated by shared ideals and co-
creation and collaboration. There are already trends in that direction, with the rise in startups facilitating 
co-living communities. Our children's new living communities will not be selected based on how close it 
is to the subway, or ranked school or fancy postcode. Physical distance will become less relevant with 
self driving and virtual work environments. Education is increasingly moving away from a physical 
school as a prerequisite for success. Our children seek not to be rooted in the notion of ownership, but to 
be free to collaboratively consume and to uproot as they grow through experiences in life, and explore 
new experiences that they can add to their repertoire of recorded life stories. All this in a bid to 
demonstrate their uniqueness while still always having common ground with the others around them. 
They are looking for physical and social vibrancy at a 
throw, tied through shared curiosity and 
dynamic co-creation. Their families will be built through a different set of lenses from ours, and we 
EFTA01050454
--- PAGE 3 ---
should learn from them, perhaps no longer centered around isolation and bloodlines but through 
connection and shared values. What is the new Olive Tree? Let's let them show us. 
Our children will fall in love across national borders... more than ever before... we will have to solve for 
immigration. They aren't looking to put their trust in faceless corporations and governments that control 
where they can go and who they can talk to. They want freedom from the platforms that are 
manipulating their actions based on a conflicting need to satisfy advertisers. They are looking for 
transparency, portability and true participatory politics. And as they find themselves, they find their 
voices and as they share those voices, new nations will be built in those digital spaces, no longer with 
lines etched in Mother Earth. This is an activist generation, unafraid of voicing their distaste with the old 
world, but as yet without the leverage to effect systemic change. Just you wait. The areas of investment 
related to the blockchain, where we can now fathom new systems of trust and transparency and measures 
of value separate from fiat currency are already being screamed for by some in our generation. When 
Generation N begin to take over the technological tools, we will see an explosion of innovation related to 
the opportunities these technologies create. It's already happening. We already see the old world seek 
advertising dollars not from businesses that just want to sell products, but increasingly from businesses 
that see the opportunity in selling experiences. The new engagement metrics to look for are now different 
from the old world of DAUs and MAUs. Let's not lock our children's faces to screens for the sake of it. 
While many talk about software eating the world, I choose to put stock in software (specially static scale 
out logic systems) becoming irrelevant. That instead data eats the world. An ever growing store of 
human knowlege and individual experiences. The opportunities will no longer be in building software 
platforms, because the world is moving away from ubiquitous software. We used to design for 
interoperability. Software that could be put on multiple touchscreens from multiple vendors. But as we 
live out the trend of tighter software and hardware coupling and personalization (advanced 3D printing) 
we will increasingly ditch our smartphones the same way we ditched our keyboard and mouses, and we 
will surround ourselves with personalized hardware that is always on, always connected, always 
listening and always informing. And these hardware pieces will have software designed just for them. 
They will plug into a common set of data stores. And while we may see some Al and ML algorithms at 
scale, those opportunities will pale in comparison to the value of immutable, accessible and responsible 
data stores for our and our children's data. In the future of work, teams will be formed dynamically, 
comprised of various experts who have honed their craft and knowledge within their own communities, 
coming together in diversity to build in unity. Value will come from providing Gen Z with insights rather 
than info. 
These are now opportunities to pursue globally. China has shown they can outinovate on hardware (look 
at DJI), and as we move towards closer coupling of HW/SW systems, and more ubiquitous connected 
devices, the innovation will come from the actual builders of these products and methods of 
collaboration and not all will reside within the US. Even more so as it relates to physical spaces, events 
and communities. I see the vast number of opportunities all around the world and through Binary I am 
pursuing them aggressively. Help. Let's support more together. 
These opportunities are likely not to be found thriving where regulations are still built by leaders and 
populations that fear change and have built systems to safeguard the worldview of the zero sum game of 
a hoarding and accumulation mentality. A system that thrives on flow is unlikely to spring up where flow 
is blocked by individuals and groups in current positions of power that strive to hold on to that power. 
The business model for government is broken, accelerated by rise in automation and robotics. If they 
can't tax output tied to land, what will they attempt next? A new system that is consciously connected 
and that encourages flow also encourages the surrender of power, and assumption of it only when called 
on to do so. The smart, mission driven entrepreneurs will go where they can thrive. 
We are each individual neurons of humanity. And now we are able to fire synapses across the whole. 
Where tribes of the past existed as a utility to safeguard our physical genes, the tribes of our future exist 
as a utility to evolve our minds and consciousness. While we are physically separate, our souls yearn to 
EFTA01050455
--- PAGE 4 ---
be of one mind. That is our design. 
As I stated earlier, there are also several cautions in this shift. If we build these busineses with too much 
dependency on the systems of old, we may plunge our children into a far scarier dystopian future. If we 
do not turn our voices into action in liberating our data from the systems of old, or if we give in to the 
petty products that are designed to distract us from discovering our individual gifts by focusing on our 
need for ego validation, we run the risk of placing the power of these new technologies in the hands of 
institutions that are designed to aggregate rather than distribute. To hoard and build stagnation instead of 
give and encourage energy flows. 
We have a moral obligation to build a future that our children want, not one that we want for ourselves or 
for them. We should hand them our stories, and hand them new tools, good tools, many tools. And watch 
them build. Our beliefs will not be their beliefs. They should not be. They should be free to decide what 
those are for themselves. And now they have some of the tools to do so collectively. Let's not fuck it up 
for them 
I kinda thought it appropriate to copy a little paragraph I wrote last weekend while I was watching the 
setting sun as my family was enjoying some cheese and crackers downstairs, intended for my team but 
since we are all in this together, I figure that's all of you too. 
"This is not a manifesto. You, who are reading this already know the truth of non-truths: totality is 
defined by everything in absence, and we are all part of the same. In that, we accept all things as they 
are, yet understand what they could be for now and beyond. 
Our focus is on the human species, and the action drivers that exist on the spectrum of fear and love, 
which bears stating are not in opposition. As of 2017, human actions at the individual and tribal levels 
have had primary motivations closer to the fear-driven end of the spectrum. This includes the fear of 
scarcity (of time, resources, knowledge), fear of insignificance (of life purpose, actions, emotions), fear 
of separation (from empathy, growth, emotions). 
The current dominant world system has developed from an amplification of fear driven actions. 
A new emergent world system will amplify love driven actions, and be an alternative to the current 
system. They will necessarily operate in parallel till the energy transfer is complete. If it becomes 
complete. 
The technological age as we have come to call it is a powerful force for this, including digital technology 
such as the Internet and Al, as well as practiceable and organic technologies such as meditation, 
phenethylamines and tryptamines. These technologies enable connectivity to occur outside of physical 
space. They usher in a new age of coalescence and coordination, core components of what is needed for 
us to bring about a new emergent world. 
Our responsibility is to design or invest in the components that bring this connectivity to more people. 
Let's continue to support the good work our network is doing." 
Sent from my iPhone

as Collaborative Non-Conformity, a global affinity and dependence on diversity, and see it as the 
EFTA01050463
--- PAGE 2 ---
simple confluence of increasing worldwide connectivity through technology and growing individual 
accountability across our communities. In other words, public and referenceable identities and 
experiences, and access to more tools than ever that allow us to communicate, trade, self-publish and 
provide feedback on those identities and experiences. 
I see this as an opportunity to witness a practical participatory economy take shape, with a generation 
of empowered individuals operating outside the shadows creating a new framework for humanity to 
amplify and celebrate our differences on this beautiful playground of spaceship Earth, and perhaps 
beyond. To be respectful of nature as they lay the Fabric of Wisdom on the Information Age. But, it 
could also go the other way (I will mention without caution on that below). 
//What is happening?// 
While our generation and the ones before us began our lives building friendships and finding our 
tribes in physical space, our children, or Generation (N)ow as I call them, are starting their lives and 
finding their tribes in digital space. They find like-mindedness earlier, and find them from a larger 
pool. As a generation, this empowers them to embrace their uniqueness more than ever before 
possible, at a younger age than ever before. 
Gen N are also entering this world with a keener awareness of being part of a connected species. Up 
until now, we have each come into this world concerned primarily with our navigable physical space. 
As we have become more connected, our voices travel further and our information comes from 
across the world, through channels we have curated for ourselves (the age of mass media is 
increasingly behind us). Generation Z is the last transition generation. After them, a majority of souls 
coming into physicality will grow up primarily communicating, exchanging ideas, and forging 
relationships with others beyond geographical or nationalistic boundaries. 
While we have lived and built mostly physical lives and sought to bring expressions of them online, 
Gen N are beginning their time on Earth with digital identities, with corporations and governments 
charting their growth and experiences without their conscious choice to have it be so. Their new 
battle is not primarily for money but instead more social relevance and credibility in the form of an 
audience and owned digital content. Oh the stress! 
As this digital shift brings our identities online, Gen N are developing a global accountability of their 
actions, as everything is increasingly digitized and stored (Internet of Things, ubiquitous sensors, 
etc). 
They are also starting to have access to a global hive mind to look to for solutions, as we each 
become publishers, and crowdsourced data feeds into the variety of machine learning algorithms and 
A.I. projects that seek to answer our health, economic and scientific questions. 
//Where must we invest? - Building trust in an untrustworthy world// 
Is our obligation and burden to build and leave tools and structures that we think support Generation 
IN ability to thrive in this seemingly complex world they are coming into? No! That's obnoxious to 
think we know what's best for them. Our obligation is to watch them, and learn from them. Allow 
them space to build trust with one another. This is a generation that will lead us into a collective 
living environment that is conscious and tolerant as long as we don't hold them hostage to our old 
ways of thinking about our definitions of personal and collective success! 
What we should invest in and conserve are spaces for them to play within and between tribes, to 
explore the connectivity with each other and nature and the self-actualization they will inevitably 
confront. Because we are humans, and we are physical. Until we can mimic a completely realistic 
physical environment in virtual space (hrmm... but worth trying), they need real places to commune 
EFTA01050464
--- PAGE 3 ---
and celebrate their digital tribes. They are already asking for this. Look at the rise in meetup culture 
and festival culture and youth conferences all across the planet. They are already looking for their 
playgrounds to meet with their digital communities that share the same appreciation for music, art, 
science, nature and everything else (scarily even VidCon). I'm looking actively to support the 
creation and protection of these spaces and events. 
They will seek out places to live together. Aggregated not by our old world notions of what matters, 
tied often to productivity and economics (fuck co-working), but instead aggregated by shared ideals 
and co-creation and collaboration. There are already trends in that direction, with the rise in startups 
facilitating co-living communities. Our children's new living communities will not be selected based 
on how close it is to the subway, or ranked school or fancy postcode. Physical distance will become 
less relevant with self driving and virtual work environments. Education is increasingly moving away 
from a physical school as a prerequisite for success. Our children seek not to be rooted in the notion 
of ownership, but to be free to collaboratively consume and to uproot as they grow through 
experiences in life, and explore new experiences that they can add to their repertoire of recorded life 
stories. All this in a bid to demonstrate their uniqueness while still always having common ground 
with the others around them. They are looking for physical and social vibrancy at a 
throw, 
tied through shared curiosity and dynamic co-creation. Their families will be built through a different 
set of lenses from ours, and we should learn from them, perhaps no longer centered around isolation 
and bloodlines but through connection and shared values. What is the new Olive Tree? Let's let them 
show us. 
Our children will fall in love across national borders... more than ever before... we will have to solve 
for immigration. They aren't looking to put their trust in faceless corporations and governments that 
control where they can go and who they can talk to. They want freedom from the platforms that are 
manipulating their actions based on a conflicting need to satisfy advertisers. They are looking for 
transparency, portability and true participatory politics. And as they find themselves, they find their 
voices and as they share those voices, new nations will be built in those digital spaces, no longer with 
lines etched in Mother Earth. This is an activist generation, unafraid of voicing their distaste with the 
old world, but as yet without the leverage to effect systemic change. Just you wait. The areas of 
investment related to the blockchain, where we can now fathom new systems of trust and 
transparency and measures of value separate from fiat currency are already being screamed for by 
some in our generation. When Generation N begin to take over the technological tools, we will see 
an explosion of innovation related to the opportunities these technologies create. It's already 
happening. We already see the old world seek advertising dollars not from businesses that just want 
to sell products, but increasingly from businesses that see the opportunity in selling experiences. The 
new engagement metrics to look for are now different from the old world of DAUs and MAUs. Let's 
not lock our children's faces to screens for the sake of it. 
While many talk about software eating the world, I choose to put stock in software (specially static 
scale out logic systems) becoming irrelevant. That instead data eats the world. An ever growing store 
of human knowlege and individual experiences. The opportunities will no longer be in building 
software platforms, because the world is moving away from ubiquitous software. We used to design 
for interoperability. Software that could be put on multiple touchscreens from multiple vendors. But 
as we live out the trend of tighter software and hardware coupling and personalization (advanced 3D 
printing) we will increasingly ditch our smartphones the same way we ditched our keyboard and 
mouses, and we will surround ourselves with personalized hardware that is always on, always 
connected, always listening and always informing. And these hardware pieces will have software 
designed just for them. They will plug into a common set of data stores. And while we may see some 
AI and ML algorithms at scale, those opportunities will pale in comparison to the value of 
immutable, accessible and responsible data stores for our and our children's data. In the future of 
work, teams will be formed dynamically, comprised of various experts who have honed their craft 
and knowledge within their own communities, coming together in diversity to build in unity. Value 
will come from providing Gen Z with insights rather than info. 
EFTA01050465
--- PAGE 4 ---
These are now opportunities to pursue globally. China has shown they can outinovate on hardware 
(look at DJI), and as we move towards closer coupling of HW/SW systems, and more ubiquitous 
connected devices, the innovation will come from the actual builders of these products and methods 
of collaboration and not all will reside within the US. Even more so as it relates to physical spaces, 
events and communities. I see the vast number of opportunities all around the world and through 
Binary I am pursuing them aggressively. Help. Let's support more together. 
These opportunities are likely not to be found thriving where regulations are still built by leaders and 
populations that fear change and have built systems to safeguard the worldview of the zero sum game 
of a hoarding and accumulation mentality. A system that thrives on flow is unlikely to spring up 
where flow is blocked by individuals and groups in current positions of power that strive to hold on 
to that power. The business model for government is broken, accelerated by rise in automation and 
robotics. If they can't tax output tied to land, what will they attempt next? A new system that is 
consciously connected and that encourages flow also encourages the surrender of power, and 
assumption of it only when called on to do so. The smart, mission driven entrepreneurs will go where 
they can thrive. 
We are each individual neurons of humanity. And now we are able to fire synapses across the whole. 
Where tribes of the past existed as a utility to safeguard our physical genes, the tribes of our future 
exist as a utility to evolve our minds and consciousness. While we are physically separate, our souls 
yearn to be of one mind. That is our design. 
As I stated earlier, there are also several cautions in this shift. If we build these busineses with too 
much dependency on the systems of old, we may plunge our children into a far scarier dystopian 
future. If we do not turn our voices into action in liberating our data from the systems of old, or if we 
give in to the petty products that are designed to distract us from discovering our individual gifts by 
focusing on our need for ego validation, we run the risk of placing the power of these new 
technologies in the hands of institutions that are designed to aggregate rather than distribute. To 
hoard and build stagnation instead of give and encourage energy flows. 
We have a moral obligation to build a future that our children want, not one that we want for 
ourselves or for them. We should hand them our stories, and hand them new tools, good tools, many 
tools. And watch them build. Our beliefs will not be their beliefs. They should not be. They should be 
free to decide what those are for themselves. And now they have some of the tools to do so 
collectively. Let's not fuck it up for them 
I kinda thought it appropriate to copy a little paragraph I wrote last weekend while I was watching 
the setting sun as my family was enjoying some cheese and crackers downstairs, intended for my 
team but since we are all in this together, I figure that's all of you too. 
"This is not a manifesto. You, who are reading this already know the truth of non-truths: totality is 
defined by everything in absence, and we are all part of the same. In that, we accept all things as they 
are, yet understand what they could be for now and beyond. 
Our focus is on the human species, and the action drivers that exist on the spectrum of fear and love, 
which bears stating are not in opposition. As of 2017, human actions at the individual and tribal 
levels have had primary motivations closer to the fear-driven end of the spectrum. This includes the 
fear of scarcity (of time, resources, knowledge), fear of insignificance (of life purpose, actions, 
emotions), fear of separation (from empathy, growth, emotions). 
The current dominant world system has developed from an amplification of fear driven actions. 
EFTA01050466
--- PAGE 5 ---
A new emergent world system will amplify love driven actions, and be an alternative to the current 
system. They will necessarily operate in parallel till the energy transfer is complete. If it becomes 
complete. 
The technological age as we have come to call it is a powerful force for this, including digital 
technology such as the Internet and Al, as well as practiceable and organic technologies such as 
meditation, phenethylamines and tryptamines. These technologies enable connectivity to occur 
outside of physical space. They usher in a new age of coalescence and coordination, core 
components of what is needed for us to bring about a new emergent world. 
Our responsibility is to design or invest in the components that bring this connectivity to more 
people. Let's continue to support the good work our network is doing."

From: Hugo Hodge
To: Richard Kahn
Cc: Amy Dempsey
Subject: Re: GSJ 
Date: Mon, 03 Apr 2017 14:16:19 +0000 
>, "jeffrey E." cjeevacation®gmail.com> 
Good morning All, 
We made the site visit on Friday morning. I would like to make a few observations on the proposals. Note that I 
will not have exact dollar amounts until I get some land and sea distances that we I am working on with Amy. 
I. We visited the dew desired landings on GSJ and they appear to be feasible. 
2. We visited the proposed landing on St. Thomas where the existing landing from LSJ is located at Great Bay. It 
appears that you can save significant money on both the submarine cable length and the installation as I believe 
Amy can float that cable for you. However, I must caution you that this solution does not offer the redundancy or 
reliability as landing in Red Hook. You would have to obtain an easement to extend the pad, presumably from 
the hotel, and this design would produce what we call in industry a single point of failure and a dependency on 
one feeder. The design I proposed with the landing in Red Hook offered two separate landings coming from 2 
different feeders. The most redundant and reliable design. Additionally. it provides a design that would allow for 
the sale of one of the islands without complications relative to the power system design if it ever came into play 
years from now. 
3. The option brought to my attention of serving GSJ by connecting the radial feed to LSJ and using the 
proposed on land conductor to the site is very unreliable and not recommended. 
4. My recommendation, if cost savings from the original design is desired, would be to run the submarine cable 
from Red Hook to GSJ. Order the reel of cable for the GSJ-LSJ interconnection with the order but store it for a 
later time and defer the on land cable from LSJ to the site on GSJ until a later date. 
I can be available to discuss these findings. When a final decision is made, if an alternate to the design approved 
by WAPA is selected, I will have to formally submit a new drawing and obtain a new approval. Additionally, we 
need to give Mr. Bryan the approval to get the switchgear as soon as possible to avoid extended lead times 
becoming a factor. 
Best Regards, 
HH

Letter I would like to send to Harry. 
I am re-sending the letter below, since it wasn't answered, and I would like to clear up this very painful affair --
which I do not understand -- as quickly as possible. 
To repeat the essentials, concerning the marital trust, there are several options discussed in earlier letters. I won't 
again review the fact that the marital trust was set up so that funds would be available to the survivor, with what 
remains going to the children. Though that is a fact, it seems that your interpretation is different, though you 
have not responded to my repeated inquiries about that. But let's put that side. The options seem to be these: 
I. You can resign and then you will have no further obligations and no fears about further liabilities from which 
you have to be protected. We can then return to the situation before I appointed you as trustee in my place. I 
will be the trustee. As before, there will be no problems about fiduciary responsibility, no concern about liability, 
no problem about funds that are needed, no lawyers or intrusive inquiries into finances. 
Furthermore, you can be assured that after I die most of the trust will be added to your inheritance. Now that the 
radical depletion of my IRA has been overcome, and I have responsible financial advisers, there will be limited 
occasion to access the Trust, and my advisers will ensure that there are no distributions from it without my 
knowledge and that other requirements will be honored with regard to interest and other matters. 
2. We can adopt your suggestion, leaving you in charge, in which case you will ensure that the entire Trust will go to you. To repeat the very 
simple logic, a few years ago, before I found out about it, my IRA was being very seriously depleted. Half of the mandatory withdrawal was 
being distributed to family, the other half was being used to pay management fees and taxes for the entire estate. Therefore, in order to pay 
Alex's medical bills and expenses for Wellfleet, I had to make extra withdrawals with an onerous tax payment. And since I also needed 
something to live on, I had to make still more withdrawals, with even further onerous tax payments. At that point I asked Max to release 
some funds from the marital trust for tax relief. You refused, demanding an intrusive and insulting financial accounting that no one with a 
shred of dignity would accept -- particularly under these remarkable circumstances. It follows that any request without such very clear 
justification will also be refused. So you can be assured of receiving the entire Trust. I also suggested an improvement: you can take all of it 
right now and we can dissolve the Trust. 
3. We can pursue my suggestion: divide the Trust right now and dissolve it. To repeat, there are some arcane tax issues, but can easily be 
resolved, as your lawyer can explain to you, with common consent among the beneficiaries -- which means your 
EFTA01050849
--- PAGE 2 ---
consent. 
4. I will repeat: "I could pursue legal measures to have the tnist used in the manner in which it was intended. I could also look 
into the disbursements that have been made to family members (so I have learned) without informing me, and could look into 
why I haven't been receiving any income from the trust for years (until I finally raised the question), and why investments were 
made the way they were done, yielding long-term retums that would be of no use for me, highly irregular for an elderly person 
— which, as I wrote you, greatly surprised financial advisers I consulted when I finally began to pay attention. And, 
furthermore, why I never received any statements about what was going on for years, until I finally asked what is going on with 
the trust. And perhaps other matters that evidently concern you, as shown by your request for protection for past actions. But 
I haven't yet shifted to your domain and still retain some illusions about family relations." 
These appear to be the options. I hope we can settle this quickly. As I have repeatedly explained with no response, I cannot 
expect what my father was able to enjoy, but at least I would like to end this particular horror as quickly as possible.

As usual, you ignored everything I wrote and and are pursuing your own agenda. But this letter is nevertheless 
very helpful. I've been asking you repeatedly to clear the air and say exactly what you want instead of evading it 
in one way or another, and this does come close to that. It also finally explains clearly what I did not want to 
believe about your refusing my request for some funds for taxes a few years ago 
You no doubt recall the circumstances. Unknown to me, my financial advisers had arranged to rapidly deplete 
my main source of support, my IRA, by distributing half of the mandatory withdrawal to family members and to 
use the rest for paying management fees and taxes for the entire estate. That meant that when I paid Alex's 
expenses, I had to withdraw over the limit, with exorbitant taxes. Same with any other funds for any family 
matters, and with Wellfleet payments well after I stopped using the house, again with exorbitant taxes. Of course 
I also needed to live, so that meant more withdrawals with exorbitant taxes. Under those conditions I requested 
some tax relief from the marital trust -- which, of course, was established on the understanding that it would be 
available to the survivor. 
Your reaction, to my amazement, was to refuse, even under these remarkable circumstances, by imposing absurd 
conditions that no one with a shred of dignity could accept, no concem of yours. Of course, no such questions ever were on 
even the remote horizon when I was trustee, before choosing you to replace me, or on any other occasion when I arranged for 
funds to go to you, either as an ample inheritance or for regular expenses. 
Your letter now makes your reasoning very clear. Your proposal is that you should remain in total control, evidently a matter of 
great importance for you. And following your principles, as exhibited with crystal clarity under even the extreme circumstances 
just described, you can ensure that the funds in their entirety will go to you, though I suppose in your kindness you might relax 
your strict regimen slightly when the day comes, as it must, when I am no longer in a position to retain a shred of dignity and 
to refuse an intrusive and humiliating interrogation. 
However, there is a simpler way to realize your objectives, even more fully. You can resign as trustee — of course possible, 
just as I did when I appointed you. We can then agree that you receive the entire funds right now, instead of waiting until I die, 
so that you can use them right now for whatever purposes you like. Plainly that's more efficient, and even more lucrative for 
you than your suggestion. 
It's true that this is one possible proposal, as you suggest. 
Another proposal is the one I suggested. True, there are some arcane tax issues, but these can easily be resolved, as your 
lawyer can explain to you, with common consent among the beneficiaries -- which means your consent. 
There are, of course, other possibilities. I could pursue legal measures to have the trust used in the manner in which it was 
intended. I could also look into the disbursements that have been made to family members (so I have learned) without 
informing me, and could look into why I haven't been receiving any income from the trust for years (until I finally raised the 
question), and why investments were made the way they were done, yielding long-term returns that would be of no use for 
me, highly irregular for an elderly person -- which, as I wrote you, greatly surprised financial advisers I consulted when I finally 
began to pay attention. And, furthermore, why I never received any statements about what was going on for years, until I

finally asked what is going on with the trust. And perhaps other matters that evidently concern you, as shown by your request 
for protection for past actions. But I haven't yet shifted to your domain and still retain some illusions about family 
relations. 
There are other matters that I've written to you about several times, with no response, which means I presume 
that you do not want to hear them. They don't specifically have to do with this matter, so if you have gotten this 
far in the letter, you can stop here. But they are on my mind, and I want to clear the air — if anyone wishes to 
look. 
My father could die in peace, knowing his children would ensure that his wife would be taken care of. I don't 
have that luxury. 
No lawyers or words were necessary. It was simply obvious that we would hand over to her what there was of 
an inheritance, the house and everything in it. And of course we were very pleased that he had joy and 
companionship in his last years. 
Valeria and I are very happy together, apart from what you are doing, which is naturally extremely painful. She 
left her friends and family, and a professional life. I have almost no pension, as I described, and it terminates 
when I die. Accordingly, I have to deal with concerns that my father, luckily for him, never had to consider. 
The situation is not only extremely painful, but in fact surreal. I could never have imagined that anything like 
this would happen in my last years.

From: Noam Chomsky

Letter I would like to send to Harry. 
I am re-sending the letter below, since it wasn't answered, and I would like to clear up this very painful affair --
which I do not understand -- as quickly as possible. 
To repeat the essentials, concerning the marital trust, there are several options discussed in earlier letters. I 
won't again review the fact that the marital trust was set up so that funds would be available to the survivor, 
with what remains going to the children. Though that is a fact, it seems that your interpretation is different, 
though you have not responded to my repeated inquiries about that. But let's put that side. The options seem 
to be these: 
I. You can resign and then you will have no further obligations and no fears about further liabilities from 
which you have to be protected. We can then return to the situation before I appointed you as trustee in my 
place. I will be the trustee. As before, there will be no problems about fiduciary responsibility, no concern 
about liability, no problem about funds that are needed, no lawyers or intrusive inquiries into finances. 
Furthermore, you can be assured that after I die most of the trust will be added to your inheritance. Now that 
the radical depletion of my IRA has been overcome, and I have responsible financial advisers, there will be 
limited occasion to access the Trust, and my advisers will ensure that there are no distributions from it without 
my knowledge and that other requirements will be honored with regard to interest and other matters. 
2. We can adopt your suggestion, leaving you in charge, in which case you will ensure that the entire Trust will go to you. To repeat the 
very simple logic, a few years ago, before I found out about it, my IRA was being very seriously depleted. Half of the mandatory 
withdrawal was being distributed to family, the other half was being used to pay management fees and taxes for the entire estate. 
Therefore, in order to pay Alex's medical bills and expenses for Wellfleet, I had to make extra withdrawals with an onerous tax payment. 
And since I also needed something to live on, I had to make still more withdrawals, with even further onerous tax payments. At that point 
I asked Max to release some funds from the marital trust for tax relief. You refused, demanding an intrusive and insulting financial 
accounting that no one with a shred of dignity would accept -- particularly under these remarkable circumstances. It follows that any 
EFTA01050866
--- PAGE 2 ---
request without such very clear justification will also be refused. So you can be assured of receiving the entire Trust. I also suggested an 
improvement: you can take all of it right now and we can dissolve the Trust. 
3. We can pursue my suggestion: divide the Trust right now and dissolve it. To repeat, there are some arcane tax issues, but can easily 
be resolved, as your lawyer can explain to you, with common consent among the beneficiaries -- which means 
your consent. 
4. I will repeat: ^I could pursue legal measures to have the trust used in the manner in which it was intended. I could also 
look into the disbursements that have been made to family members (so I have learned) without informing me, and could 
look into why I haven't been receiving any income from the trust for years (until I finally raised the question), and why 
investments were made the way they were done, yielding long-term returns that would be of no use for me, highly irregular 
for an elderly person — which, as I wrote you, greatly surprised financial advisers I consulted when I finally began to pay 
attention. And, furthermore, why I never received any statements about what was going on for years, until I finally asked 
what is going on with the trust. And perhaps other matters that evidently concern you, as shown by your request for 
protection for past actions. But I haven't yet shifted to your domain and still retain some illusions about family relations? 
These appear to be the options. I hope we can settle this quickly. As I have repeatedly explained with no response, I 
cannot expect what my father was able to enjoy, but at least I would like to end this particular horror as quickly as possible. 
Earlier letter below. 
D 
As usual, you ignored everything I wrote and and are pursuing your own agenda. But this letter is nevertheless 
very helpful. I've been asking you repeatedly to clear the air and say exactly what you want instead of evading 
it in one way or another, and this does come close to that. It also finally explains clearly what I did not want to 
believe about your refusing my request for some funds for taxes a few years ago 
You no doubt recall the circumstances. Unknown to me, my financial advisers had arranged to rapidly deplete 
my main source of support, my IRA, by distributing half of the mandatory withdrawal to family members and 
to use the rest for paying management fees and taxes for the entire estate. That meant that when I paid Alex's 
expenses, I had to withdraw over the limit, with exorbitant taxes. Same with any other funds for any family 
matters, and with Wellfleet payments well after I stopped using the house, again with exorbitant taxes. Of 
course I also needed to live, so that meant more withdrawals with exorbitant taxes. Under those conditions I 
requested some tax relief from the marital trust -- which, of course, was established on the understanding that 
it would be available to the survivor. 
Your reaction, to my amazement, was to refuse, even under these remarkable circumstances, by 
imposing absurd conditions that no one with a shred of dignity could accept, no concern of yours. Of course, no such 
questions ever were on even the remote horizon when I was trustee, before choosing you to replace me, or on any other 
occasion when I arranged for funds to go to you, either as an ample inheritance or for regular expenses. 
Your letter now makes your reasoning very clear. Your proposal is that you should remain in total control, evidently a matter 
of great importance for you. And following your principles, as exhibited with crystal clarity under even the extreme 
circumstances just described, you can ensure that the funds in their entirety will go to you, though I suppose in your 
kindness you might relax your strict regimen slightly when the day comes, as it must, when I am no longer in a position to 
retain a shred of dignity and to refuse an intrusive and humiliating interrogation. 
However, there is a simpler way to realize your objectives, even more fully. You can resign as trustee — of course possible, 
just as I did when I appointed you. We can then agree that you receive the entire funds right now, instead of waiting until I 
die, so that you can use them right now for whatever purposes you like. Plainly that's more efficient, and even more 
lucrative for you than your suggestion. 
It's true that this is one possible proposal, as you suggest. 
Mother proposal is the one I suggested. True, there are some arcane tax issues, but these can easily be resolved, as your 
lawyer can explain to you, with common consent among the beneficiaries — which means your consent.

There are, of course, other possibilities. I could pursue legal measures to have the trust used in the manner in which it was

My father could die in peace, knowing his children would ensure that his wife would be taken care of. I don't

No lawyers or words were necessary. It was simply obvious that we would hand over to her what there was of

Valeria and I are very happy together, apart from what you are doing, which is naturally extremely painful.

terminates when I die. Accordingly, I have to deal with concerns that my father, luckily for him, never had to 
consider. 
The situation is not only extremely painful, but in fact surreal. I could never have imagined that anything like

I will check with DOJ on Monday, but until the Administrator for the Board comes back on April 10, I don't think we will 
get someone to give us an update. The bids you received on the sheds, from a model cost point of view, may not be 
completely out of whack considering the amount of concrete foundations that have to be done, particularly in the first 
floor storage room between the two buildings that we are creating. That space is entirely concrete. The footprint of space 
being built out is approximately 10,200 SF. If you include the Buck Steel quotes with the estimate, you end up with a total 
cost of $744,345.00 or approximately $73.00/SF. This is a very fair cost for the amount of square footage created and the 
logistics of constructing on the cay. We can solicit additional proposals but I don't believe they will be much less, if at all, 
than the bid from Elderfield Roberts. 
The pavilion has a footprint of approximately 2,400 SF. Given the quality of construction and design, it is fair to assume it 
will have a rough unit cost of $400.00/SF or cost $960,000.00. If we develop the area below the main level shown in the 
elevations, that cost will increase by another $250,000.00. I know we are still trying to resolve the screening of the pool 
on the west side, but I feel the pavilion itself is fairly resolved. What do you think? 
JPW

Noam — 
Thank you for your reply. As you indicate that you are not being represented by counsel I will reply directly to you, with 
a copy to Rich (as you suggest). Please consider: 
1. 
As a starting point, let me note that I think you and Rich may have misunderstood (at least initially) the terms of 
the settlement that Harry proposed through his attorney. Rich and I discussed this in a call about 10 days ago and I'm 
hoping that misunderstanding has been cleared up, but as I'm not a party to your exchanges (and Rich's exchanges) 
with Harry's attorney I can't be sure. I'm also not certain whether the terms of the proposed settlement have changed. 
All I can say for sure is that characterizing the offer as one in which distributions to you cannot exceed $100K per year is 
not consistent with my understanding of what has been offered. 
The reason why the proposal is too outrageous to discuss has nothing to do with the technicalities of the handout 
that Harry is graciously offering. I'll review the background, once again. 
As I've discussed before, the Marital Trust was established in Carol's name for tax purposes. The obvious intention, 
clearly understood by Carol and me, and of course Eric Menouya, was that it would be available to the survivor --
Carol we assumed -- and then what remains would go to the beneficiaries. The idea that we intended that Carol 
would control "her" funds and I would control "mine" is too ludicrous to discuss, though I understand the legalistic 
conjuring that can be adduced to reach this conclusion. 
When I appointed Harry to replace me as trustee, I took for granted that he would handle the trust as I had. His 
behavior since, and this latest proposal, make it very clear how wrong that assumption was. This proposal calls for 
him to be in complete charge, which means, as he has shown, that I can only plead for some funds by accepting 
conditions that he knows I will not accept. You recall, I presume, that this was true even when I faced an enormous 
tax bill because my IRA was being depleted for the benefit of the family. 
To refresh your memory, let me repeat again what was happening with my IRA until I learned about it. There is a 
mandatory withdrawal. Half was being distributed to family. The other half was being used for taxes and 
management fees for the entire estate. In order to pay Alex's medical expenses, and to pay $50,000 a year for rent 
and upkeep on the house in Wellfleet that we had given to the children and that I was barely using, I had to 
withdraw extra funds from the IRA, with the onerous tax burden. The same when I withdrew something to live on. 
Under these circumstances, Harry refused to release funds from the Trust for tax relief without onerous and 
humiliating conditions that he knew I would not accept. Easy to predict what might happen under less extreme 
conditions. 
For such reasons, Harry's proposal is, as I said, too outrageous to discuss. 
2. 
As you know, Harry's attorney has commenced a legal action that is intended to facilitate my resignation and the 
appointment of a successor trustee to take my place. Since you've wanted me removed for some time and since I've 
said (from the first time you and I met) that I only wanted to serve as trustee if all the family members wanted me to 
serve, I'm looking forward to resigning as soon as the court determines how I am to do so and how my successor is to 
be selected. 
3. 
Given that my replacement is impending, it might be worth waiting until my successor is in place before 
responding to my requests for financial disclosure, as it's possible that my successor won't share my views as to what 
the trustee of the trusts needs to know before making decisions about distributions. Likewise, if my successor will be 
identified soon it might make sense for me to hold off on any distributions and leave it to the new trustee to work with 
you on figuring all of this out. In this regard I'm kind of a "lame duck" trustee, wouldn't you say? 
EFTA01051163
--- PAGE 3 ---
4. 
To the extent that you want to push forward while I remain the trustee, let me again state the basis for financial 
disclosure by you. It is that, as trustee, I owe a duty to you and I owe a duty to your children (as the remainder 
beneficiaries of the trusts). For the present my primary duty is to you and it is to distribute to you all income earned by 
the trusts, net of expenses, 
Until I asked about the matter recently, I am aware of no income distributed to me earned from the trusts. I cannot 
be sure, because I also do not recall having received any accounting of what is happening to the trusts, including 
distributions from them to others (or as required, to me). Could you then please send me the records on these 
matters. 
and to distribute to you (or pay on your behalf) additional monies as reasonably needed to the extent that your income 
from other sources is not sufficient to support your reasonable expenses. 
Notwithstanding your statement that "As for the claim about concern for my later years, that has been thoroughly 
refuted" it has not been refuted in the context of my trusteeship and it remains my duty to consider distributions in 
light of the possibility that you will have a reasonable need for distributions from the trust for many more years, and 
perhaps in increasing amounts, depending on your circumstances in the future. 
I am approaching 90. I'm not going to live forever. You know how much money is in the trust. How could there 
possibly be a concern about it being depleted? You know my lifestyle very well. Perhaps you recall the meeting in 
my office when you explained to me that I was going to have to cut back on expenses, specifically to sell my boat, as I 
did. None of this makes any sense. 
5. 
As for the specifics of disclosure, what I need to consider is (a) what your income was in 2017, since that was the 
basis for the tax payments you seek to have reimbursed, (b) what your income is likely to be this year and going 
forward, (c) what your expenses were in 2017 and are likely to be in 2018, and (d) whether any of your income (or other 
resources) are being used for purposes that the trust cannot support (such as gifts to third parties). So far, Rich has 
provided me with some rough information about your 2017 expenses. There are some gaps in that information, but 
nothing that can't be cleared up pretty easily (I think). Rich has also assured me that you have not made any gifts that 
have diminished your resources and I assume you would confirm that to me. What I don't have at this point is enough 
information about your income, so that I can consider what the gap is between your expenses and your income, which 
is the gap the trusts might help to close up. With respect to your income in 2017, all I can see is that your income tax 
obligations seem to be much higher than they were previously. I'm assuming that reflects a jump in income from (i) the 
profit made on the sale of the condominium, and (ii) large withdrawals from your IRA. If you want to provide me with 
more information (bearing in mind what I noted in item #3, above) then information about your 2017 income and what 
your income is likely to be this year is what I most need. 
There is a very simple reason for the income tax obligations. The depletion of the IRA that I reviewed again above 
imposed a huge tax burden, which we were still attempting to deal with in 2017. After Harry's refusal to release 
some funds from the trust to pay the exorbitant taxes resulting from what was happening, I of course had to 
withdraw funds from the IRA to pay taxes on the whole estate, incurring a new exorbitant tax burden. Despite some 
small relief later from the trust after I had repeatedly pointed this out, it carried over through the 2017 tax bill. So 
for that reason, taxes were extremely high. That curious episode is at last finally over, leaving many questions 
unresolved about what was happening while I was paying little attention, relying on advisers to ensure that matters 
were proceeding appropriately.

Conference. I assumed that Wendy was working directly with Stuart. 
Two weeks ago, I embarked on an India tour and spoke in Agra and got to meet their Supreme Leader. 
Vishal directed me to people that I was to personally invite to Shanghai and did so on behalf of the 
Conference. I also gave talks in Chandigarh, Delhi, and Mumbai and promoted attendance to the Conference 
at each place. 
Regarding what appears to be this final break, I only became aware of it when I received this message from 
Wendy: 
This was my introduction to the current "situation." While I have no idea as to how things got so off track 
(NOR WAS I INVOLVED), the wording of the message above sounds to me a lot like an ultimatum. Wendy 
was understandably worried as at the time, she was taking the financial risk, had placed deposits, and invited 
senior officials. When Stuart wrote me asking for suggestions, my recommendation was to focus on the 
event at hand, and worry about the investment till later. I also recommended to Wendy to just focus on the 
event at hand. However, unlike an academic conference, Wendy was committing considerable resources to 
make the conference grand and it was highly doubtful that it would recoup costs. Wendy considered many 
options alternatives, but my recommendation to her was to see TSC through. 
I spent some time talking to James Tagg who was working toward reconciling the situation and it was agreed 
that the only thing that would diffuse the situation is if Stuart and Wendy spoke. I have previously offered, 
with James, to mediate a conversation between Wendy and Stuart. I also suggested that each person write 
their grievances in bullet point format (for which they feel requires an apology as a precondition to real-time 
communication. I also suggested that by taking the investment idea off the table, the lawyer could be 
dismissed. However that has not come about over the last few days. 
My intention in taking the time to write this are two fold. 
I) To clear my name of Stuart's accusations. I introduced Stuart to Wendy and helped to facilitate the 
collaboration. Until the above message from Wendy, I have not been involved in any of the discussions or 
negotiations between Wendy and Stuart. It is both unfair and inappropriate for Stuart to make such 
accusations to my friends and others. Not only do I feel that my efforts are taken fore granted, I am being 
unfairly blamed for the consequences. 
2) To the best of my knowledge, Wendy plans are: 
a) To organise her own conference later in the year.

stories that trigger the sympathetic nervous system and result in actions driven by fear / need / desire. Given

On Mar 29, 2017, at 8:18 AM, james I personal genius < 
wrote: 
Yeah, he'd emailed me asking which network should he be using. 
Basically, devices won't "float" between networks hosted by different vendors. So if you have a linksys router 
in your bedroom and an Apple router in your kitchen, your iPhone continues talking to whichever device it 
talked to first until it completely drops that signal and searches again -- even if the network names are the 
same. 
The 6th & 3rd floor network names are different to make that clear (and so I can make sure the Apple TV isn't 
joining the 5th floor Apple router by mistake). 
That's what's happening with the screenshot he sent. That computer is talking to the floor below, not the eero. 
The eero tested at 100/12. 
The eero is the only system that works on 6 to the Apple TV. Apple & google won't. 
I'll discuss it with him.
